description: verifyEvmTxAgainstIntent (base-signer.mjs) does NOT bound the amount a compromised/malicious Skip route can actually pull to the driver-supplied `amount` -- it bounds it to APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS/MAX_SWAP_BASE_UNITS ($100), which is 5x SWAP_MAX_USD ($20, constants.mjs:16, the driver's independently-capped per-invocation ceiling that requiredBaseUnits/`amount` is ALWAYS <=, per driver.mjs:174-175/swap-need.mjs:41-46). This is the exact crux the sprint-2 fix's own doc comment claims to have closed and gets wrong. Mechanism: (1) ensureApprovalsSettled (base-signer.mjs:327-348), called from getNextNonce() before every leg-0 submission, sends a REAL on-chain approve() for APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS ($100) to whatever `spender` address the (possibly attacker-controlled) Skip probe route names, and only if `have < APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS` -- once the allowance reaches $100 it is NEVER lowered/revoked, so after the very first swap the wallet carries a STANDING $100 on-chain allowance to that spender for the rest of this instance's life (module header itself documents this as intentional: '$100 gives headroom for many swaps ... before a re-approval is ever needed', base-signer.mjs:88). (2) verifyEvmTxAgainstIntent's gate 3 (base-signer.mjs:177-184) only checks that `required_erc20_approvals[0].amount` -- a SELF-REPORTED JSON metadata field in Skip's HTTP response -- equals the driver's `amount` exactly; it never decodes `evm_tx.data` to verify what the entry-point/router contract's OWN internal logic will actually pull via transferFrom. (3) The post-gate allowance check (base-signer.mjs:413-418) only asserts `currentAllowance >= approval.amount` (i.e. $100 >= $20, trivially true), never `==`. (4) Gate 1 (base-signer.mjs:151-161) only rejects a BARE top-level transfer()/transferFrom() selector; it does nothing for an arbitrary router/entry-point call, which is the route's LEGITIMATE shape (module header, line 107-109) and therefore cannot be rejected outright. Combined: a fully-malicious/compromised Skip response can set `to` = the already-$100-approved spender, report `required_erc20_approvals[0].amount` == the current small `amount` (passing gate 3 exactly), and embed arbitrary calldata whose on-chain execution (msg.sender == the spender contract, from USDC's perspective) invokes `transferFrom(wallet, attacker, 100_000_000n)` -- pulling the FULL standing allowance, not the reported/intended amount. None of the four gates, nor the post-gate check, decodes or bounds the ACTUAL calldata's pull amount. This directly contradicts base-signer.mjs:143-144's own claim ('required_erc20_approvals[].amount ... is the only amount [the spender] CAN pull via transferFrom once approved') -- that claim is false: the spender CAN pull up to the full standing on-chain allowance ($100) regardless of what the metadata field says, because the metadata field is never cross-checked against the actual calldata or against how much allowance was ACTUALLY granted for THIS specific swap (none was -- the allowance is a pre-existing, amount-independent standing grant). Net effect: worst-case loss under a fully-malicious Skip route is bounded to $100 (APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS), NOT to `amount` (max $20) -- a real, unacknowledged 5x loss-amplification vector on the highest-risk money-moving module in this repo.
